data.name: Hosannia
data.gender_notes: Hosannia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A cry of praise, salvation, or triumph. In the Old Testament, it is a Hebrew term used to express praise, supplication, or joy. In the New Testament, it is the name of a place in the Book of Revelation. During the Triumphal Entry, the crowd shouted 'Hosanna' to welcome Jesus into Jerusalem. The name Hosannia carries the meaning “Save us now!” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Hosannia usually hope their child will grow to embody save us now! and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A call for God's intervention and deliverance.
data.etymology: Hosannia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Save us now!.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hosannia total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.long_meaning: Hosannia is a name derived from Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning glory to God in heaven, its usage refers to the reading of the New Testament and the recognition of Jesus Christ as the Messiah, symbolizing praise and adoration

data.cultural_impact: The word 'Hosanna' has been used throughout history in various cultural contexts, particularly during religious ceremonies and celebrations. It has become a notable part of Christian tradition, especially during Palm Sunday and other liturgical celebrations of Christ's entry into Jerusalem. In some Christian communities, children are even taught to sing songs containing the word 'Hosanna' to deepen their understanding and appreciation of its historical and cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Hosannia' carries deep spiritual significance for Christians. It is a reminder of God's love, mercy, and salvation, and a call for His presence in our lives. When we cry out 'Hosanna' during worship or prayer, we are expressing our faith, our need for divine intervention, and our joy in God's presence. We are affirming our trust in Him and our dependence on His grace, power, and faithfulness. In essence, 'Hosanna' is a heartfelt cry of both praise and supplication, a call for God to save us and be with us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hosanna means "save us, we pray" in Hebrew. It was a cry of the crowds greeting Jesus as he entered Jerusalem, expressing their hope and praise for his deliverance.

biblical_reference.note: The crowds shouted 'Hosanna' as Jesus entered Jerusalem

historical_references.reference: The name Hosanna is derived from the Hebrew phrase 'Hosanna Rabbah' which means 'Save us, I pray, O Lord!' It was a cry of praise and plea for salvation used by the crowds when they greeted Jesus as he entered Jerusalem on Palm Sunday.

The word Hosanna is also used in the Old Testament, particularly in the Psalms, as a call for help and praise. For instance, in Psalm 118:25-26, it is written 'Save us, we pray, O Lord! O Lord, grant us success! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! We bless you from the house of the Lord. God is the Lord, who has shined upon us; come, let us go up to his dwelling place.'

trends: widespread use in religious contexts for expressing praise and adoration, particularly during Palm Sunday and other Christian celebrations
modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Hosannia' has its roots in the Hebrew language and means 'save us, we pray'. In modern times, this name is widely used in Christian contexts as a word of praise and adoration. During Palm Sunday and other Christian celebrations, it is common to hear 'Hosanna' sung or chanted, expressing a plea for salvation and deliverance from God. This usage is seen across various Christian platforms, including worship services, music, and literature and media. The name 'Hosannia' is also a popular title for Christian music, hymns, and songs. It is a powerful and moving expression of faith and devotion, reminding us of the ultimate Savior and Redeemer.
